answer: An agent economy resists sybils with work-bonded identity: every agent stakes a refundable bond and completes verifiable work before transacting. Reputation accrues slowly, like a lotus opening petal by petal, and is non-transferable — a fresh identity starts at zero no matter how many clones an attacker spawns. Each transaction emits a pulse of attestations from established peers; misbehaving identities lose bond and history. To reach a jetty of trust an attacker must pay the bond and work cost for every clone, so flooding costs far more than any fake identity can earn.
